content.title: About
content.content: Canned spinach cooked with vegetable oil consists of finely chopped spinach leaves that have been blanched and sealed in airtight jars with added oil. The product is ready to eat and retains most of the nutrients of fresh spinach.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Spinach belongs to the Amaranthaceae family and is one of the most nutrient‑dense leafy greens.
Canning allows storage for 2‑3 years without significant loss of flavor or most vitamins.
The oil in the jar enhances absorption of fat‑soluble vitamins A, D, E and K found in spinach.
Spinach is used in traditional dishes worldwide: in Russia in salads, in Italy in pasta, in Japan in omelets.

items.title: Rich in vitamin K
items.content: Vitamin K is essential for normal blood clotting and bone health.

items.title: Source of iron
items.content: Iron from spinach helps maintain hemoglobin levels and prevents anemia.

items.title: Contains antioxidants
items.content: Lutein and zeaxanthin protect the eyes from age‑related degeneration.

items.title: Low‑calorie food
items.content: One cup of canned spinach provides about 30 kcal, making it a great choice for weight‑controlled diets.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: Dietary fiber promotes regular bowel movements and a feeling of fullness.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Canned foods often contain added salt; people with hypertension should monitor portion size.

items.title: Allergy to vegetable oils
items.content: Some individuals may react to the oil used in the can.

items.title: Fat oxidation
items.content: Prolonged storage can cause oil to oxidize, affecting taste and aroma.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Spinach can be eaten straight from the jar, added to salads, soups, pasta, omelets, or used as a filling for pies. If desired, drain the oil and rinse the leaves with cold water.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the unopened jar in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. After opening, keep refrigerated and consume within 3‑4 days.
